27	
28	## Judges' verdicts
29	
30	### Judge 1
31	
32	Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.
33	
34	Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
35	
36	Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.
37	
38	Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.
39	
40	### Judge 2
41	
42	Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.
43	
44	## Designers' rationales
45	
46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
47	
48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
49	
50	Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.
51	
52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.
53	
54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.
59	
60	## Studies

194	### quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo (priority 1)
195	
196	**technique.** Validation harness: purged k-fold with embargo keyed on label end time, Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV) backtest paths, CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (PBO), deflated Sharpe ratio, minimum backtest length, stationary block bootstrap of sessions, and a shared trials ledger for every candidate gate from H1-H5 and these studies.
197	
198	**what_it_answers.** Are the in-sample improvements of any candidate gate (rooms ST7/ST8, H2 regime, H3 volume, H4 levels, H5 rule lists, the studies below) larger than what picking the best of N trials produces by chance on 823 (5m) or a few thousand (1m) SETUPs? Which candidates have earned the single out-of-sample look? How many candidates can this sample afford before selection bias dominates?
199	
200	**method.** (1) Splitter module in the scratchpad, importable by every study: groups = 12 contiguous session blocks on IS (about 85 sessions each); purge = drop training SETUPs whose label lifetime [setup_i, label_exit_i] intersects the test block's bar range (label_exit_i = the label's own exit bar: the 15:25 bar for the intraday label, fnd_exit_i for the engine label which runs to 70 sessions on 5m and would purge a lot, one more reason to train on the intraday label); embargo = 3 sessions after each test block (longest feature memory: room age 3 sessions on 5m, vol_med60, range36, BSADF window 1 session). Exposes split(X, y, groups) so sklearn cross_val_predict and CalibratedClassifierCV(cv=iterable) accept it. (2) CPCV with N = 12 groups, k = 2 test groups: 66 purged train/test splits assembled into 11 full backtest paths per model; each study reports the distribution over paths (median, 5th percentile) of its kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference, control percentile and winner recall, not one number. (3) Trials ledger (CSV, append-only): one row per candidate configuration any study or H1-H5 evaluates, including every threshold a greedy search tries: candidate id, config JSON, label used, per-session IS net vector of the kept book, n_kept, script sha. (4) CSCV / PBO: matrix M candidates x T = 1,026 IS sessions of kept net per session; S = 16 blocks, all C(16,8) = 12,870 IS/OOS partitions; per partition the IS-best candidate (by mean kept net per session and, separately, by the kept-vs-skipped statistic) and its relative OOS rank; PBO = share of partitions with logit(rank) < 0; also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope. (5) Deflated Sharpe ratio for each finalist: per-session Sharpe of the kept book, deflated by the expected maximum Sharpe under M trials (variance of Sharpe across the ledger), with skew and kurtosis of per-session net; p-value reported. (6) Minimum backtest length for the observed Sharpe and M, checked against T. (7) Stationary block bootstrap of sessions (Politis-Romano, mean block 10 sessions, 2,000 draws, seeded) for confidence intervals of kept-vs-skipped differences and control percentiles; this is the harness's only generative component. 217	
218	**technique.** Meta-labelling: a secondary model over the Foundation primary model, trained on triple-barrier and intraday label variants with return-attribution (|net|) sample weights, uniqueness weights where labels overlap, optional time decay; bagged depth-limited trees and a depth-3 interaction-constrained gradient booster as ceilings, a binned logistic scorecard as the deployable form, distilled to a rule list of at most 8 depth-3 rules.

220	**what_it_answers.** Given that Foundation already chose side and entry, what is P(the trade pays after costs | as-of context) at the SETUP bar, which SETUPs should be skipped, and does a gate trained to preserve the large winners (the user's 'avoid only loss trades') beat the frozen ST7/ST8 rooms gate and the session-matched random control on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, on IS out-of-fold and once on OOS? 222	**method.** Inputs: features.parquet per timeframe through an allowlist of as-of columns (97 numeric plus one-hot or count encodings of fz_read, fz_gate, fz_block_reason, fz_branch, dir, hv3_dir, card_out_side, last_bos_dir, last_choch_dir, last6_kinds); bars.parquet to recompute labels. Primary training label = L1 binary (net > 0); L0/L2/L3 are robustness labels, every gate is evaluated on L1 because that is the book ST13/ST14 will trade (square_off 15:25). 238	### quant-ml-canon-feature-importance (priority 3)
239	
240	**technique.** Clustered feature importance (MDA and MDI on correlation clusters, single-feature importance per cluster) under purged cross-validation, the orthogonal-feature sanity check, fractional differentiation (fixed-width FFD with a hand-coded ADF choice of d*) as a candidate feature family, and TreeSHAP interaction values for discovering the 2-3-feature interactions that justify depth-2/3 rules.
241	
242	**what_it_answers.** Which of the 143 as-of columns (97 numeric, 114 pairs with |rho| > 0.9, so raw importances would be split by substitution) carry information about the intraday Foundation outcome; which at most 8 feature clusters the ST13/ST14 keys should be built from and what their config-expressible representative is; whether the canon's fractionally differentiated price features add anything beyond the ATR-normalised distances already in the table; which feature pairs interact strongly enough to justify a depth-2/3 rule, so that H5's rule search can be restricted (fewer trials, lower PBO).
243	
244	**method.** (1) Feature set: as-of numeric plus encoded categoricals as in the meta-label study; NaN kept for HGB, a missing-indicator plus median for bagging; columns with > 40% NaN dropped and listed. (2) FFD family: on log close per timeframe, fixed-width fractional differentiation for d in {0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0} with weight cut 1e-4 (window length recorded); ADF regression with constant and 2 lags hand-coded in numpy (MacKinnon 5% critical value -2.86 embedded and cited); d* = smallest d whose ADF statistic on IS bars is below the critical value; features at the SETUP bar: ffd_close_d*, its z-score against a 60-bar rolling std, the same on log volume; plus the CUSUM-filter counts from the regime study when available. (3) Clustering: Spearman correlation on IS, distance sqrt(0.5 (1 - rho)), scipy average linkage, cut chosen by silhouette in the 20-40 cluster range; every cluster gets a representative chosen by config-expressibility (integer counts and card fields before ATR ratios before raw points). (4) Model and protocol: BaggingClassifier of depth-limited trees on the L1 label with |net| weights under the harness splitter (12 purged, embargoed blocks). Clustered MDA: permute all features of a cluster jointly on the test fold, 5 permutations x 12 folds, record the drop in OOF weighted log-loss and, separately, the drop in OOF kept-vs-skipped expectancy at the fold's tau (the metric that matters); report mean and std across folds; a cluster is kept only when its mean MDA exceeds one std. MDI from the same forest summed per cluster; SFI: each cluster alone under the same CV. (5) Orthogonal check: PCA on standardised IS features, weighted Kendall tau between MDI rank and eigenvalue rank; a low tau is reported as a warning that the importance may be noise-fitting. (6) Interactions: xgboost max_depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05 on the same folds restricted to the top-40 features; shap.TreeExplainer(...).shap_interaction_values on OOF rows; pairs ranked by mean |interaction|; the top 5 pairs with their split points from the tree structure become candidate depth-2/3 rules for H5 and the distillation step. (7) Stability: repeat (4) per IS year (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and report the rank correlation of cluster importances across years; a feature whose importance is not stable across years is not proposed as a key. Output: importance tables per timeframe, the shortlist (<= 8 clusters with representatives and definitions cited by README name), the FFD verdict, the interaction pairs.

247	
248	**compute.** FFD over 445k 1m bars x 10 d values with windows up to about 1,000 weights via numpy convolution: 1-2 minutes; ADF: 10 small regressions; clustering on 97 x 97: instant; MDA: 12 fits of a 300-tree bagging on <= 5k rows plus about 40 clusters x 5 permutations x 12 folds = 2,400 predict calls on <= 500 test rows: 5-8 minutes; xgboost and SHAP interactions on <= 5k rows x 40 features, depth 3: about 1 minute, interaction tensor 5k x 40 x 40 float64 = 64 MB (the full 100-feature tensor would be 400 MB, hence the top-40 restriction); total about 15 CPU-minutes per timeframe, peak under 500 MB.

327	
328	**technique.** Offline contextual bandit with full-information rewards, solved as cost-sensitive policy learning: value-maximising depth-limited policy trees (Athey-Wager / Zhou-Athey-Wager) and cost-proportionate weighted gradient boosting, with the policy value computed exactly (direct method, no IPS) and distilled to a rule list
329	
330	**what_it_answers.** Which Foundation SETUPs to take and which to skip, by regime / time / volume / level / card context, chosen to maximise INR value (not accuracy), and whether the learned gate beats the session-matched random gate and the frozen ST7/ST8 gates on kept-vs-skipped expectancy rather than by trading less.
331	
332	**method.** Inputs: fz_v3/minute/setup_features.parquet (5,326 rows, 118 as-of columns) and fz_v3/5minute/features.parquet (1,012 rows, 143 as-of columns). Reward table per SETUP: r_take = fnd_net (primary variant recomputed from bars with a 15:25 square-off on the entry session, stop as hard floor; secondary = the engine's own exit as built), r_skip = 0. Every gate pi has exact value V(pi) = mean(pi(x) * r_take); baselines: Foundation (pi = take), ST7/ST8 (st7_traded / fzpos_kind), session-matched random at the same per-session count. Learners on IS only: (A) exact depth-1 and greedy depth-2/3 policy trees whose split criterion is the policy value (sum of r_take over the take-leaf), min leaf 100 SETUPs (1m) / 40 (5m), implemented in numpy over ~110 features x 30 quantile thresholds; (B) HistGradientBoostingClassifier on y = sign(net) with sample_weight = |net| winsorised at the 1st/99th percentile (Zadrozny-Langford-Abe cost-proportionate reduction; with two arms and full information this is the regret-optimal reduction), policy = take iff P_w(win) > 0.5, plus HistGradientBoostingRegressor on winsorised net with policy take iff E[net|x] > tau, tau swept post hoc from out-of-fold predictions; (C) distillation: fit a depth-<=3 DecisionTreeClassifier (min leaf 100) to (B)'s out-of-fold decisions and extract <= 8 conjunctive rules; report fidelity to (B) and the distilled policy's own CV value. Selection on IS CV only: maximise kept-minus-skipped mean net subject to kept share >= 20% and kept n >= 300 (1m) / 80 (5m); also report the value with the top 1% winners removed (heavy tail: 1m winners median 1.8k, p90 10k INR). Diagnostics: SHAP (TreeExplainer) on (B) for the drivers; winner recall and loser precision; per-hour and per-regime kept share. 372	**technique.** Session-block stationary bootstrap, combinatorially symmetric cross-validation (PBO), Reality-Check/SPA multiplicity control over the whole candidate set, generative null tapes (session-bootstrap tapes and a GMM-Markov regime generator re-run through engine.run + fz.run), and adversarial validation for drift

374	**what_it_answers.** Whether any gate / exit / sizing rule from studies 1, 2, 4, 5 has an edge that survives (a) resampling of sessions, (b) the number of candidates searched, (c) tapes generated from a null with no swing-structure memory (the edge should vanish there; if it does not, the gain is engine mechanics or cost avoidance), and (d) feature drift inside IS; and therefore whether a key may be written to strategy_13/14.json at all.
375	
376	**method.** (a) Stationary bootstrap (mean block 5 sessions, 2,000 draws) of the per-SETUP outcome table on IS: for EVERY candidate policy evaluated in studies 1/2/4/5 (the full logged search set, not just the selected ones) the distribution of kept-minus-skipped mean net and of the session-matched control percentile; White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA p-value for "the best of M candidates beats the benchmark" with benchmark = Foundation and benchmark = the random gate at the same k. (b) CSCV / PBO: 16 contiguous session blocks, all C(16,8) = 12,870 IS/pseudo-OOS combinations, rank candidates in each half; PBO = share of combinations where the IS-best ranks below median out; also the deflated (haircut) expectancy after M trials. (c) Synthetic tapes fitted on IS bars only: (i) session-bootstrap tapes: whole sessions resampled with replacement, price level chained through session returns, gap distribution kept; (ii) GMM-Markov tapes: GaussianMixture (4-6 components, full covariance) on per-bar (log return, log volume ratio to the session-clock median, range/atr14, close position in bar) with a first-order Markov chain on the component labels fitted by transition counts, sampled per session with the time-of-day volume profile; (ii) preserves volatility clustering and volume shape but not swing/CHoCH memory, so it is the null. 1	# null_tapes_drift: synthetic null tapes (c) and adversarial drift validation (d)
2	
3	DESIGN_PANEL decision-making-3, parts (c) and (d), with both judges' fixes: (a) / (b) live in `harness.py`; the null tapes run on 5 minutes (20 full-length tapes per generator) and on 1 minute (8 one-year tapes per generator, RSS checked); the segment bootstrap is Judge 1's second null; the IS-vs-OOS adversarial check is not run here (oos_once.py post-mortem). No gate search, no OOS row read. Tape numbers never enter the ledger; the three reference gates on the real tape are ledger rows of family `null_tapes_drift/real_ref`. Scripts: `gen_tapes.py`, `tapes.py`, `run_tapes.py`, `drift.py`, `write_findings.py`; logs `run_5minute.log`, `run_minute.log`, `drift.log`, `topup_5minute.log`, `topup_minute.log`. **Repair round (section 11)**: the adversarial refuters found the engine locked out on part of the tapes; the certificate is now read on healthy tapes (the first-build numbers stay published beside it), `tapes.py` refuses time proxies, the two mechanical gates are labelled as what they are, and the missing `go_no_go` item is stated as a program-level gap.
4	
5	## 1. Definitions (fixed before the numbers)
6	
7	- **Unit / label / statistic** as the harness: a Foundation SETUP taken under the L1 (15:25) book; kept-vs-skipped difference of mean net (INR per unit); the session-matched random control percentile (`fz_report.random_control`, 2,000 draws); permutation p; block sign count. On a tape the statistic is computed by `harness.metrics` on a `harness.Table` built from the tape's own `features.parquet` / `trades.parquet` / `sessions.parquet` (`tapes.load_tape`, a copy of `harness.load` pointed at the tape folder). Every tape row is IS (the tapes carry IS calendar dates).
8	- **Three reference gates** (all as keep masks): `frozen_st7_st8` = keep where `fz_traded` (the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as it traded on that tape); `choch2_skip` = skip where `n_choch_since_bos >= 2` (mechanical reference gate 1); `sl_above_median_skip` = skip where `sl_dist_atr` > the tape's own IS median (mechanical reference gate 2). The two mechanical gates were **fixed in `tapes.py` before any tape was scored**; they are reference points for the engine-mechanics check, not candidates, and appear in no registration file (BRIEF H2 names the family `n_choch_since_bos >= k` without k; the stop-distance gate exists only here). Their ledger rows (section 3) carry the earlier wording 'pre-registered' in the config text, which this file supersedes. The engine-mechanics check: a gate on stop distance or CHoCH counts can read non-zero on a memory-free tape through the engine itself (Judge 2), so its null is not 0.
9	- **Generators** (fitted on IS bars only, `gen_tapes.py` docstring): *session bootstrap* (whole IS sessions with replacement, level chained through the drawn session's open-to-close path and a gap drawn from the IS gap distribution); *segment bootstrap* (30-bar clock-aligned blocks from random IS sessions, re-based and chained, same gap draw); *GMM-Markov* (GaussianMixture 4-6 full-covariance components by BIC on the z-scored per-bar vector (log return, log volume ratio to the clock median, range/atr14, close position), first-order Markov chain on the labels, per-session sampling with the clock volume profile, OHLC rebuilt consistently, samples clipped to the IS range per dimension). Full-length sessions only (375 / 75 bars); the real IS tape's short sessions are excluded from the pools (listed in `fit_<tf>.json`). Tapes are written in the near-month CSV format and pushed through `build/build.py --path` (engine.run with the Foundation rules, fz.run with the frozen ST7/ST8 block, L0 and L1 pricing, the same 261-column feature table).
10	- **Engine health of a tape / per-tape poor-null flag (repair round; `tapes.tape_health`)**: an IS session is *frozen* when the engine's protected level `prot` (bars.parquet) does not change inside it, equals the previous session's last value and no CHoCH occurs; a *dead run* is a run of frozen sessions longer than the real tape's longest such run (5minute 68, minute 69 sessions); *dead share* = sessions inside dead runs / sessions. A tape is **healthy** when dead share < 0.2 AND its SETUP rate is >= 0.333 x the real tape's. The flag reads bars / events / sessions / setups only, never a label or a gate statistic. **Tape sets**: `gates` = the **certificate**: the first DESIGN_N (20 / 8) healthy tapes per generator by seed index k (`tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)` default; when the first build held fewer, the next seeds k = 20, 21, ... were generated until the count was reached: `run_tapes.py --target-healthy`); `gates_all_original` = the first build (k < DESIGN_N) with its locked tapes (the numbers the first version of this file reported); `gates_healthy_original` = the first build's healthy tapes only. The pass rule (section 7) reads the certificate set.
11	- **Null distribution** = per timeframe, generator, gate and tape set: p5 / p50 / p95 / mean / min / max of the tape diffs, the share of tapes with diff > 0, p50 / p95 of the control percentile, the real-tape value and its percentile among the tapes. **Comparison** (DESIGN_PANEL (c), Judge 1's go/no-go): the real-tape difference must be above the null-tape 95th percentile; here that is read on the two memory-free nulls (GMM-Markov and segment), with the session bootstrap as the stability read (share of tapes with the real diff's sign).
12	- **Reality check** per generator: within-session per-bar log-return std (bps) and excess kurtosis, autocorrelation of |r| at lags 1-5 (pairs inside a session), CHoCH / BOS / SETUP / L1-unit counts per session, the raw L1 book, the frozen gate's kept share, the final price level and median ATR14, over every tape built (the generator as it is) and over the certificate tapes; a generator whose median SETUP rate is outside [1/3, 3] x the real rate is flagged a poor null (generator level); the per-tape flag above is the tape level.
13	- **Adversarial validation (d)**: HistGradientBoostingClassifier IS-early (2021-10-01..2023-09-30) vs IS-late (2023-10-01..2025-12-31) on `harness.design(T)` of the real tape, IS rows; pooled out-of-fold AUC under `harness.purged_splits` (12 blocks, purge by exit bar, 3-session embargo); chance = 20 label permutations; variant A = all as-of columns, variant B = without time proxies (|Spearman rho| >= 0.9 with `session_idx`); SHAP (TreeExplainer) ranking on B with the direction of drift.

215	### 5c. Engine lock-out on the null tapes (repair round; `tape_health.csv`, `tapes/<tf>/<gen>_<k>/tape_health.json`)
216	
217	**Mechanism** (engine.py, protected level): the protected level `prot` is the last unbroken *candidate* swing of the current trend; a swing becomes a candidate only when it lies on the far side of the AVWAP anchored at the last trend flip (`qualifies`: a low below that AVWAP in an up-trend, a high above it in a down-trend). On a driftless random-walk tape a long one-directional walk leaves the anchored AVWAP far behind, no new swing qualifies, `prot` freezes at the last candidate, and a CHoCH (a close beyond `prot` against the trend) becomes unreachable while BOS (a break of the last swing high / low with the trend) continues at its normal rate; no CHoCH means no SETUP. The real market returns to its anchored levels often enough that the real tape's longest frozen run is 68 / 69 sessions (5minute / minute); the locked tapes carry runs of 99-932 sessions. A run can end when the walk wanders back (a recovered mid-tape lock-out; the tail rule alone misses these) or last to the end of the tape.

1	# exit_policy — FINDINGS (IS only, 2026-09-29)
2	
3	Study `decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp` (DESIGN_PANEL, both judges' fixes) with BRIEF addendum 6: the managed replay is `lab.manage` / `lab.price_trade`, never a second implementation. Entries are frozen (every IS unit of `harness.load(tf)`, label L1, both timeframes); only the exit changes. No OOS row was read.
4	
5	## 1. Definitions (fixed before the numbers)
6	
7	- **Entries**: the L1 units, entry at the SETUP bar's close in the SETUP's direction; 1 min = Strategy 1 rules (prev_swing stop), 5 min = Strategy 2 rules (choch_candle stop).
8	- **Square-off bar**: the last bar of the entry session opening at or before 15:25 (`lab.eod_cut`); **cap** = min(square-off bar, the contract's last candle) — every comparator is cut there.
9	- **Foundation stop**: `features.sl`, engine touch convention (open beyond the stop -> fill at the open; wick touch -> fill at the stop; a session's first bar -> the close). Identical to `lab.manage`'s stop (proved on every IS trade, section 2).
10	- **Extended trajectory** (learners A / B, the floor oracle): bars entry+1 .. J_end, J_end = the Foundation stop bar when it fires before the cap, else the cap. Exits before J_end are at the bar's close; at J_end the exit is the stop fill or the cap close. The engine's next-CHoCH exit is not applied (Exo-MDP: the tape does not react, so every exit policy is replayable).
11	- **Value**: net INR per trade per lot = `lab.price_trade` arithmetic (lot 65, 5 pts slippage per side, `lab.trade_charges(ZERODHA_NFO_FUT)` on the slipped prices); a 3-lot ladder is reported per position and per lot (position net / 3); selection and every comparison use per lot.
12	- **Oracle (free)**: the best close exit over entry+1 .. cap with no stop (an upper bound for any close-exit policy; a target filled intrabar can exceed it by at most that bar's range). **Oracle (floor)**: the best exit on the extended trajectory, ties -> earliest (learner B's target). **Exit regret** = oracle - policy.
13	- **Random-exit control**: exit at a uniformly drawn bar of entry+1 .. cap at its close, 2,000 seeded draws (`fz|exit`); a policy's percentile = share of draws whose mean net per lot is below the policy's (+ half the ties).
14	- **CHoCH against**: an `events.parquet` CHoCH with i > entry, i <= t, direction opposite to the position (known at its own bar under touch rules). **Time stop N**: exit at the close of bar entry+N if still open.
15	- **Cut convention (learner C)**: the time stop and the CHoCH-against exit are a post-processing cut of `lab.manage`'s tranches: every tranche whose lab exit bar is later than the cut bar exits at the cut bar's close instead; a tranche the lab closed at or before the cut bar keeps its exit (the stop / target on the cut bar is assumed first, as `lab.manage` assumes the stop first on a candle); with both cuts on, the earlier bar wins.
16	- **Learner C grid** (never shrunk): stop {35, 50, 75 pts, Foundation stop via `exact_R`} x scale_out {none, 1R, 2R, 3R, 4R with 1 lot (the target is the exit), ladder 1R/2R, ladder 2R/4R with 3 lots} x trail {none, (2,1), (2,2), (3,1), (3,2), (4,1), (4,2)} x time stop {none, 30, 60, 120 bars} x CHoCH-against {off, on}; square_off 15:25 always: 196 `lab.manage` positions x 8 cuts = **1,568 variants per timeframe**, each a strategy-row dict as `rl.py` builds it (lot 65, slippage 5, `position_json`, cap = the contract's last candle as `rl.contract_end`).
17	- **Selection (C)**: nested in `harness.purged_splits` (argmax of the training fold's mean net per lot, applied to the test fold) and in the 66 CPCV splits -> 11 paths (`harness.cpcv_paths`). **Learners A / B**: 3 contiguous session-block folds (harness blocks 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-11), purge of training trades whose trajectory intersects the test fold's bars, 3-session embargo; B's p* by an inner 3-fold on the training fold; A's Q-ensembles refit per fold.
18	- **Multiplicity**: every variant and every learner is a row of the append-only `exit_ledger.jsonl` + `vectors/*.npz` (harness-compatible per-session vectors: kept = the variant, skipped / all = the Foundation L1 exit on the same entries, so `harness.pbo(vecs, 'diff')`, `harness.spa`, `harness.effective_trials`, `harness.bootstrap_ci` read them unchanged). The harness ledger (`OUT/ledger/`) is for gates; this study writes to it only the gate x exit rows of section 8.
19	- **Pass rule** for an exit candidate (adapted from `harness.GO` to a policy-vs-Foundation difference on frozen entries): nested-CV diff > 0; CPCV 5th percentile diff > 0; random-exit percentile >= 95; 12-block sign-flip one-sided p <= 0.05 with >= 8 blocks positive; **lower bound of the 90% block-bootstrap CI of the diff > 0** (`boot_ci90_lower>0`, as `harness.go_no_go` implements it: a CI entirely below 0 fails; the earlier wording 'CI excludes 0' was loose — repair, section 11); **diff with the top 1% winners removed > 0** (the harness's pre-registered `diff_top1_removed` item: the trades whose policy net is in its own top 1% are dropped, the paired diff is averaged over the rest — `diff_top1_winners_removed` in `eval_table_*.csv`); PBO <= 0.2; studentised SPA p <= 0.10 over the family (the family's vectors at the label's 2-dp precision — repair, section 11). **Disclosure (repair)**: the earlier text of this rule read 'diff with the top 1% of per-trade *gains* removed > 0' (`diff_top1_gains_removed`: the trades whose gain over the Foundation exit is in the top 1% are dropped). That variant was written after learner C's results had been read (this script's own docstring) and is negative-biased by construction: removing the top 1% of a dispersed difference lowers its mean even when the true mean is zero (its zero-mean reference, the same trim on the centred difference, is about -150 INR on 1 min). It is reported beside the pass item with that reference and is not used to decide.

1	# H1 gate audit: what the frozen ST7 (1 min) / ST8 (5 min) gates skip vs keep
2	
3	Study folder `fz_v3/out/studies/h1_gate_audit/`. Scripts `h1_gate_audit.py` (the audit, 138.6 s, log `h1_gate_audit.log` / `run.log`) and
4	`h1_posthoc.py` (one post-hoc ledger row, 18.2 s, log `h1_posthoc.log`). Every number below is IS only (SETUP date <= 2025-12-31) and
5	comes from a harness ledger row (id given) or from a CSV in this folder. Ledger sha after the audit `33170f8df9f5d50e`, after the
6	post-hoc row `1ee15dc04860b284`. All tables: `TABLES.md` (auto-generated), `h1_<tf>_<label>_*.csv`, `h1_summary.json`,
7	`h1_family_posthoc.json`; machine-readable summary `findings.json`.
8	
9	## 1. Definitions (fixed before any number was looked at)
10	
11	| term | definition |
12	|---|---|
13	| unit | a harness row: a Foundation SETUP taken under the label's book, `harness.load(tf, label)`; IS rows only (1 min L1 4,452, L0 4,502; 5 min L1 826, L0 832) |
14	| L1 / L0 | L1 = the 15:25 intraday book (primary); L0 = the engine's uncut trade (robustness) |
15	| kept | `T.F.fz_traded`: ST7/ST8 held a position on the SETUP, a TAKE or a REENTER whose R5 was the SETUP (post-SETUP; the comparator, never a feature). 745 (1 min) / 325 (5 min) IS rows on both labels |
16	| gate_at / outcome_gate | `fz_gate` as of the SETUP bar / `fzpost_outcome_gate` (REENTER when a later REENTER used the SETUP as its R5). They differ on 11 IS rows on 1 min (BLOCK -> REENTER, all filled one bar later) and 96 on 5 min (WATCH -> REENTER) |
17	| block_key | `BLOCK:<fz_block_reason>` when outcome_gate is BLOCK; `WATCH:<fz_block_reason>` when outcome_gate is WATCH and a refused TAKE branch set a reason (`leave_into_recycle`); else the outcome gate. Same definition as the local `h1_common.py`, so the cross-check is like for like |
18	| loser / winner | label net <= 0 / > 0 (costs included) |
19	| precision, recall, lift | P(loser given skipped); P(skipped given loser); precision / base loser rate (1.0 = skipping at random). `lift` is derived from the ledger row's `loser_precision` and the IS base loser rate |
20	| winner recall | count: P(kept given winner); net-weighted: kept winners' net / all winners' net |
21	| big / huge winner | label pts >= 50 / >= 100 |
22	| pts bucket | <=-50, (-50,-20], (-20,0], (0,20], (20,50], (50,100], >100 |
23	| hold bucket | label bars held: 1-5, 6-15, 16-30, 31-60, 61-120, 121-375, >375 (bars on both timeframes; a 5 min bar is five 1 min bars) |
24	| visit bin | `fz_visit_n`: 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ / none (no ref room) |
25	| variants | pre-declared, each a ledger row of family `h1/<variant>`: `frozen` (kept = fz_traded), `take_only` (fz_gate == TAKE), `take_or_reenter_at_setup` (fz_gate in TAKE, REENTER), `not_block` (fzpost_outcome_gate != BLOCK: WATCH rows treated as taken; DIAGNOSTIC, post column), `skip_only:<block_key>` (keep = block_key != key, one row per key; DIAGNOSTIC, the key uses the post outcome gate) |
26	| post-hoc | `not_block_asof` (fz_gate != BLOCK), declared after the audit's numbers were seen because the SPA best on 1 min / L1 was the post-column `not_block`; counted in the family (`h1_posthoc.py`) |
27	| FZ book | the ST7/ST8 position's own net on the kept rows (`fzpos_l1_net_inr` under L1, `fzpos_net_inr` under L0), Foundation's label net on the other rows; scored as label `<label>_fzpos` under family `h1/fz_book`. A TAKE is Foundation's own position (identical net on every TAKE row); a REENTER fills a bar later and exits by its own rules (`band_reclaim`) |
28	| selection-only book | `frozen` on the label itself: Foundation's label net on the kept rows |
29	| bridge | Foundation IS net + avoided price move of the skipped rows (-sum pts x 65) + avoided costs of the skipped rows (sum `cost_inr` = charges + 2 x 5 pts x 65 slippage) + REENTER exit delta = FZ book net (asserted to close within 0.05 INR on all four tables) |
30	| group tables | descriptive decompositions of the `frozen` ledger row by as-of and post columns; no rule was chosen on them |

207	## 8. Verdict per timeframe
208	
209	**1 min (ST7, Strategy 1 rules).** The frozen gate is not a loser filter. Its skip pile is 84.7% losers against a base loser rate of
210	84.4% (lift 1.003 on L1, 1.003 on L0); its loser recall (0.835) equals its skip share (0.833). It keeps 745 of 4,452 SETUPs and
211	throws away 82.7% of the winners' net (L1; 83.9% on L0), 84.3% of the top-decile winners and 225 of the 268 pts >= 50 winners
212	(1.48M of 1.77M INR). Kept mean -1,026 vs skipped -1,006 (diff -19.7, control 64.7th percentile, permutation p 0.86; L0 diff -129,
213	50th percentile). Its 3.73M gain over Foundation on L1 is 3.88M of avoided costs and -0.15M of selection. The late runners are the
214	`eod`-cut trades held 61-375 bars, concentrated before 09:25 (all 28 skipped) and in the 14:00 bin (58 of 62 skipped); the gate
215	keeps them at 13-18%, no better than its base rate.
216	
217	**5 min (ST8, Strategy 2 rules).** Not a loser filter either: precision 0.721 vs base 0.723 (lift 0.997; L0 0.993), recall 0.605 =
218	skip share 0.607. It keeps 325 of 826 and throws away 63.1% of the winners' net (L1; 60.3% on L0), 56.5% of the top-decile winners,
219	95 of 148 big winners (654k of 1.03M). Here the gate keeps the worse side: kept -979 vs skipped -613 (diff -366, 11.6th percentile,
220	p 0.25), and its own book is worse still (-1,108) because 97 REENTERs exit worse than Foundation's trade (-431 each). The gain over
221	Foundation (265k) is 526k of avoided costs and -261k of selection. The refused leave branch (`leave_into_recycle` 98 rows at -32,
222	`leave_vol_fail` 113 at -114, `leave_gap_quiet` 12 at +170) is where the winners it refuses sit; `skip_only:WATCH:leave_into_recycle`
223	(diff -822, 0.1th percentile, permutation p 0.088) is the family's nearest thing to a signal and it points against the frozen rule.
224	Late runners: the morning entry held to 15:25 (61-120 bars: 40 of 52 big winners skipped) and the pre-09:25 SETUPs (14 of 15).
225	
226	**H1 answer:** on both timeframes the frozen ST7/ST8 gate skips losers exactly in proportion to how much it skips; it separates
227	nothing (kept-vs-skipped difference within the random band on all four tables), it removes 63-83% of the winners' net, and its
228	whole advantage over Foundation is the cost saved by trading less. **Null result: no candidate config.**

238	coincide (different tag seeds and, locally, the FZ book rather than the selection-only book), and all of them sit in the random band.
239	Only IS files under `built/study/` were read.
240	
241	## 10. What would falsify these findings
242	
243	- A frozen-gate ledger row with diff > 0 and control percentile >= 95 on either label: the four rows here have diff -19.7 / -129.5
244	  (1 min) and -365.6 / -0.7 (5 min) at percentiles 64.7 / 50.0 / 11.6 / 28.1.
245	- A skip-pile precision above the base loser rate by more than sampling error (about +-0.012 at 3,707 skips on 1 min, +-0.04 at 501
246	  on 5 min): observed +0.003 / -0.002.
247	- A positive avoided price move (the skipped rows losing money before costs) on any table: all four are negative.
248	- A big-winner kept share above the gate's own kept share (0.167 / 0.394): observed 0.160 / 0.358.
249	- A different `fz_traded` set on a rebuild (the QUALITY.md cross-check pins 745 / 325 kept and identical FZ positions to the local build).
250	
251	## 11. Caveats
252	
253	- The group tables and the big-winner audit are descriptive breakdowns of the `frozen` ledger row; they were not used to choose a rule,
254	  and nothing in them is a kept-vs-skipped candidate except the ledger rows in section 3.
255	- `block_key`, `not_block` and the `skip_only:*` variants use the post-SETUP outcome gate (11 IS rows on 1 min differ from the as-of
256	  gate; 96 on 5 min are WATCH-as-of rows that re-entered a bar later). The as-of translation of `not_block` was scored post-hoc.
257	- The FZ-book table (`h1/fz_book`) keeps the label's exit bar for `with_label` (the splitter is not used in this study).
258	- The control percentile matches per-session counts while `diff` pools rows, so their signs can disagree for near-complete keeps
259	  (section 1); neither is read alone.
260	- L0 on 1 min runs to 70 sessions and its big winners are multi-session; the L0 columns are robustness only.
261	- `lift` is not a harness metric; it is `loser_precision` (ledger) over the IS base loser rate.

As-run script `session_stop.py` (runtime 436.1 s; log `session_stop.log`, `run.nohup`; pre-registration `preregistration.json`, sha256 `437d736cf3513a1c`, registered 2026-09-29T04:06:57; ledger sha before `4aae0153ef8a0f1d`, after `54c5d54e9b38d764`). **Repair round** `session_stop_repair.py` (runtime 5473.1 s; `preregistration_repair.json`, sha256 `56c45828cd02e985`, registered 2026-09-29T05:21:46; ledger sha before `d475f67c4ce346ec`, after `b7a266d10a48343a`; new rows `note = "repair"`). 4	
5	## 0. Result in one paragraph
6	
7	**No session memory beyond the hour effect is shown, and no `session_stop` key is proposed for ST13/ST14.** The as-run pre-registered null N1 (outcomes permuted within session x hour_bin cells over fixed positions) was rejected on 1 min (all seven tests, Holm p <= 0.0140) with a positive excess of +53 to +106 INR/trade, which the as-run study read as mean-reverting session memory. **That rejection is an artifact** (section R.1): the SETUP positions are generated by the outcomes (a trade runs until exit, winners hold ~6x longer than losers), and a memoryless generator that keeps only the clock and the durations reproduces the rejection on 100% of its streams (excess +84 to +119; 6% when the duration is made independent of the outcome). Two hindsight-free nulls replace it (section R.2): the within-hour contrast across sessions with a session-block bootstrap (N4) and the observed statistics against 2,000 memoryless streams (N3); on 1 min the min Holm p is N4 1.0000 / N3 1.0000, on 5 min N4 0.4198 / N3 0.0070: 1 min **NOT REJECTED under N3 or N4**; 5 min **INCONCLUSIVE: exactly one hindsight-free null rejects (or signs disagree)** (N3 alone rejects on `stops>=3`, 18 units, N4 does not; underpowered, not shown; the rejected contrast is positive, not the direction a stop rule needs). Branch B's grid (run under the as-run rejection) is re-judged on hindsight-free statistics only, with the session-matched control percentile set aside as a hindsight-biased comparator for sequential rules (section R.3: the same rule sits at its 0.0th percentile on memoryless streams). The family now holds 48 cells (16 hour-conditioned cells added for Judge 2's hour interaction, section R.4); the nested-CV OOF rule has diff -52.05 (top-1%-removed -61.27), the CPCV 5th percentile is -80.12, PBO 0.8248, SPA p 0.5965, and `harness.go_no_go` fails for the cell chosen on all IS both as computed and without its control check (failing: diff_top1_removed>0, kept_mean_slip8>0, cpcv_p5_diff>0, pbo<=0.2, dsr_p<0.1, spa_p<=0.10). The cells' pooled diffs sit at memoryless percentiles 18-80 and the within-hour kept-vs-skipped contrast's 90 % CI excludes zero on 4 of 48 cells (section R.5). The no-key conclusion of the as-run study stands; the memory claim, its direction and the "reverse rule" follow-up are withdrawn.
8	
9	## R. Repair round (2026-09-29): the refuters' three issues, what changed, and the repaired result

Ledger sha before the repair `d475f67c4ce346ec`, after `b7a266d10a48343a`; every new ledger row carries `note = "repair"`; the as-run rows are untouched (append-only ledger). `session_stop.py` itself was not re-run; its docstring carries a dated repair note (the as-run rows' `script_sha` is `6645343d4dfba103`, the file before the note). 164	### R.3 Issue I2: the session-matched random control is not evidence for a within-session sequential rule
165	
166	On the memoryless streams (no edge and no anti-edge possible by construction) the k = 2 / L = none absorbing rule sits at a session-matched control percentile with median 0.0 (share of streams at or below the 5th percentile 1.00) when the duration is tied to the outcome, and median 0.2 (share <= 5: 0.85) when it is independent (table R.1; the real rule's value is 0.0 for all 32 as-run cells and for the 16 hour-conditioned cells below). The control draws n_s of the N_s realized positions; N_s is only known at session end and the last positions are long winners by construction, so a rule that keeps the earliest positions loses to it whatever its merit. **`control_pct` is reported in every table but is not used as evidence for or against any cell; `harness.go_no_go` is shown as computed and without its `control_pct>=95` check.** Flag for the orchestrator: the go/no-go control check is uninformative for any sequential (position-order) rule; a comparator for such rules must be causal (a random stopping rule with the same per-session stop counts, or the memoryless generator used here).

## 7. How a candidate is evaluated on the tapes later

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '<OUT>/studies/null_tapes_drift'); import tapes
# the pass rule in one call (real_diff = the candidate's real-tape ledger row 'diff'; rules = its rule-list JSON, rules_round0.json grammar):
passed, checks, summary = tapes.null_tape_check(real_diff, '5minute', rules)      # or 'minute'
# checks = {'null_tape:real_diff>gmm_p95': (ok, p95), 'null_tape:real_diff>segment_p95': (ok, p95), 'null_tape:session_same_sign>=0.75': (ok, share)}
# summary['null_tape_diff_inr'] = {gen: {'p50', 'p95'}} is the certificate block for the key's provenance; summary['per_tape'] = every tape's metrics
# the same by hand:
for folder in tapes.tape_folders('5minute', 'gmm'):           # the CERTIFICATE set: the first 20 (5minute) / 8 (minute) HEALTHY tapes by seed index k
    r = tapes.evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules)               # (healthy=False gives every tape built, locked ones included: a sensitivity read, never the pass rule)
    r['diff'], r['control_pct'], r['kept_share']
```

**Tape set of the pass rule**: the certificate set (`tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)` default = healthy tapes, first DESIGN_N by k; section 2b lists the k of each generator). The locked tapes are never part of a pass / fail: the engine did not run on them for 22-91% of their sessions (section 5c), so their kept-vs-skipped statistic is noise on a few hundred units. Report the sensitivity read (`healthy=False`) beside it if a reader asks how the verdict moves.

**Pass rule** (DESIGN_PANEL (c) + Judge 1): the candidate's real-tape diff (its ledger row) > p95 of its own tape diffs on the GMM-Markov certificate tapes AND on the segment certificate tapes; the session-bootstrap certificate diffs carry the real sign in >= 75% of tapes. The reference nulls in `null_distributions.json` (`gates` -> `diff_p50`, `diff_p95` per generator) are the certificate values a shipped key's provenance block carries (`null_tape_diff_inr`). A rule list is never scored on the tapes before its real-tape ledger row exists (the tapes are not a search space; `tapes.py` writes nothing to the ledger).

**Program-level gap (Judge 1's binding fix, not in code here)**: `harness.go_no_go` has no null-tape item, so a gate study can pass `go_no_go` without ever running this check; `harness.py` is outside this study's write scope. `tapes.null_tape_check` returns the three items in `go_no_go`'s `(ok, value)` shape so the fix is a drop-in for the orchestrator:

```python

def go_no_go(res, tf, cpcv=None, pbo_value=None, dsr=None, spa_p=None, boot=None, null_tape=None):

    if null_tape is not None:                      # null_tape = tapes.null_tape_check(res['diff'], tf, rules)[1]
        ch.update(null_tape)                        # 'null_tape:real_diff>gmm_p95', 'null_tape:real_diff>segment_p95', 'null_tape:session_same_sign>=0.75'
    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch
```
Until that lands, the phase-3 workflow must call `tapes.null_tape_check` explicitly before freezing a candidate and record the three items in the candidate's FINDINGS and provenance.

## 8. Caveats and what would falsify these nulls

- The tapes' price level follows a random walk of drawn sessions and gaps: over 1,026 sessions some tapes end far from the real level (see `close_last` in section 5); the engine is scale-free (checked: x2 prices give identical event counts), but INR differences scale with the level, so a high-level tape widens the null in INR. This makes the p95 conservative (harder to beat); an ATR-normalised statistic would be tighter and is not the registered one.
- The GMM-Markov tape's return kurtosis is below the real tape's (a 6-component mixture cannot carry a kurtosis of ~25) and its |r| autocorrelation dies within a few bars; Judge 1's warning (a narrower-than-reality null over-rejects) is why the segment bootstrap is read alongside it and the pass rule needs both.
- The session bootstrap keeps every within-session dependence, so it is a stability read, not a null: a gate that works within the day should keep its sign there.
- Engine lock-out (section 5c, measured): on the first build the engine's protected level froze and the CHoCH stream stopped for 22-91% of the sessions on 5minute: GMM-Markov 6/20, segment bootstrap (30-bar blocks) 4/20, session bootstrap 10/20; minute: GMM-Markov 0/8, segment bootstrap (30-bar blocks) 1/8, session bootstrap 1/8 tapes (frozen-run rule; the refuters' tail rule finds 12 of 84), while BOS continued at the normal rate; the locked tapes carry as few as 78 L1 units (5minute) against 770-1211 on the certificate tapes; 430 L1 units (minute) against 613-1650 on the certificate tapes. The certificate (section 4) excludes them and was topped up to the design count with the next seeds; the first-build numbers with and without them are in section 4a (verdicts unchanged). The lock-out is itself a property of a memory-free tape (the real market returns to its anchored levels; a random walk need not), so the healthy set is conditioned on 'the engine ran', not on any gate statistic.
- `sl` (the stop price level) is in `Table.asof_columns()` although it is a raw price (|rho| 0.93 with time on 5 minutes); `n_events_asof` is a cumulative count since the data start (rho 1.0). Both are time proxies, excluded in variant B; `tapes.rule_mask` refuses them (PermissionError) and the gate studies refuse them on the real tape by rule; the harness allow-list should carry them in NOT_FEATURES (reported, not changed here).
- The 1-minute tapes are one trading year (247 IS sessions) with 8 tapes per generator: their null percentiles rest on 8 values and are wider than the 5-minute ones; the 5-minute nulls are the primary certificate, as both judges asked.
- The two mechanical reference gates are fixed reference points, not registered candidates (section 1); nothing in the ledger or the registrations depends on them.
- Falsification: if a real gate's diff sat above the GMM/segment p95 while the gate is known to be pure engine mechanics (e.g. the stop-distance gate on the real tape), the null would be too narrow; section 4 shows what the mechanical gates read on the real tape against their own nulls.
- Drift inside IS is large (section 6) and its top of the ranking is the volatility / price-level regime (5minute: `atr_bps` (lower, -0.51 sd), `atr14` (higher, +0.30 sd), `range_3h_pts` (higher, +0.27 sd), `n_rooms_alive` (higher, +0.02 sd), `hv3_ratio` (higher, +0.12 sd); minute: `atr_bps` (lower, -0.47 sd), `atr14` (higher, +0.18 sd), `days_to_expiry` (higher, +0.20 sd), `gap_pts` (higher, +0.10 sd), `sess_cumvol_ratio20s` (higher, +0.12 sd)): the tape went from ~17,500 to ~26,300 while volatility in bps fell, so every point-denominated column (`*_pts`, `atr14`, `sl_dist_pts`, `fz_band_width`, `fz_dist_band_edge_*`, `gap_pts`) drifts with the level. A rule on such a column is a level rule; the gate studies should express thresholds in the `_atr` / `_bps` forms and the CPCV path distribution, not the pooled IS number, is what a drifting IS supports.

## 9. Null result statement

This study searches no gate and proposes no candidate (`candidates: []`, `null_result: true` in the sense of 'no candidate'): it writes the certificate the gate studies compare against. The three reference gates' readings against their own nulls are in section 4b.

208	def cluster(Xa, is_mask, logf=None):
209	    Xi = Xa[is_mask]
210	    t0 = time.time()
211	    R = Xi.rank().corr(min_periods=30)          # Spearman: Pearson on ranks, pairwise-complete
212	    rho = np.nan_to_num(R.to_numpy(), nan=0.0); np.fill_diagonal(rho, 1.0); rho = np.clip((rho + rho.T) / 2, -1, 1)
213	    Dm = np.sqrt(np.clip(0.5 * (1 - rho), 0, None)); np.fill_diagonal(Dm, 0.0)
214	    Z = sch.linkage(sch.distance.squareform(Dm, checks=False), method="average")
215	    sil = {}
216	    for k in K_RANGE:
217	        lab = sch.fcluster(Z, k, criterion="maxclust")
218	        if len(set(lab)) < 2: continue
219	        sil[k] = float(silhouette_score(Dm, lab, metric="precomputed"))
220	    k_best = max(sil, key=sil.get)
221	    lab = sch.fcluster(Z, k_best, criterion="maxclust")
222	    cols = list(Xa.columns)
223	    clusters = {}
224	    for c, l in zip(cols, lab): clusters.setdefault(int(l), []).append(c)
225	    # rename clusters 0..K-1 by size then name
226	    order = sorted(clusters, key=lambda l: (-len(clusters[l]), clusters[l][0]))
227	    clusters = {i: clusters[l] for i, l in enumerate(order)}
228	    log(f"clustering: {len(cols)} features, silhouette best k={k_best} ({sil[k_best]:.4f}), clusters formed {len(clusters)}, {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", logf)
229	    # representatives
230	    coverage = 1 - Xi.isna().mean()
231	    idx = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cols)}
232	    reps = {}
233	    for ci, mem in clusters.items():
234	        scored = []
235	        for c in mem:
236	            others = [idx[o] for o in mem if o != c]
237	            cent = float(np.mean([abs(rho[idx[c], o]) for o in others])) if others else 1.0
238	            scored.append((int(c.endswith("__na")), tier_of(c, Xi), -float(coverage[c]), -cent, c))   # a missing indicator represents a cluster only when it is alone
239	        scored.sort()
240	        na, t, cov, cent, c = scored[0]
241	        reps[ci] = dict(representative=c, tier=int(t), coverage=round(-cov, 4), centrality=round(-cent, 4),
242	                        why=f"tier {t} ({'integer/boolean/one-hot/card field' if t == 0 else 'ratio' if t == 1 else 'raw points/level'}), "
243	                            f"coverage {-cov:.3f}, mean |rho| to members {-cent:.3f}" + (" (missing indicator, the cluster's only member)" if na else ""))
244	    return dict(clusters=clusters, reps=reps, silhouette={int(k): round(v, 4) for k, v in sil.items()}, k_best=int(k_best),
245	                rho=pd.DataFrame(rho, index=cols, columns=cols))

290	def choose_tau(p, net, win):
291	    """The threshold on the training fold's OOB probabilities: max kept mean net s.t. |net|-weighted winner recall >= 0.90."""
292	    tot_w = net[win].sum()
293	    best, best_val, table = None, -np.inf, []
294	    for tau in TAU_GRID:
295	        kept = p >= tau
296	        if kept.sum() == 0: continue
297	        wrec = float(net[kept & win].sum() / tot_w) if tot_w > 0 else 1.0
298	        km = float(net[kept].mean())
299	        table.append((float(tau), int(kept.sum()), round(wrec, 4), round(km, 2)))
300	        if wrec >= WREC_MIN and km > best_val: best, best_val = float(tau), km
301	    if best is None: best = float(TAU_GRID[0])
302	    return best, table

323	    K = len(clusters)
324	    # float32 storage (K x 5 x n; the fold statistics below are computed from the float64 predictions BEFORE storage). A consumer

---
## 7. The card

One row per bar, computed as of that bar and never rewritten. Fields: `zone_id` (the ref band), `visit_n`, `this_bars`, `this_vol`, `vol_na`, `first_bars`, `first_vol`, `first_vol_na`, `read`, `left_id` (the band whose LEAVE is live), `out_run`, `out_side`, `session_bar`, `gap_pts`, `wick_depth`, `last_hunt_at/dir`, `last_reject_at/dir`, `cluster_sit`, `prev_bars`, `prev_vol`, `last_leave_failed`, `in_id` (the band containing the close, nearest mid), `leave_side`, `leave_vol_ok`, `leave_kind`, `first_clock_lived`.

**Read precedence.** LEAVE (a LEAVE is live on `left_id`) → HUNT → REJECT → the inside read of the ref band's visit when the close is inside it → PENDING (the close is outside the ref band, visit still live) → NEW (no ref band).

**Inside reads.** Visit 1 reads FIRST_PRINT (`first_clock_lived` says whether it has lasted `accept_bars`). On a revisit, with B = the base visit (`volume_base`: the first visit, or the previous one): ACCEPTED when `this_bars ≥ accept_bars` and (volume is NA on either side, or `this_vol ≥ accept_vol_ratio × B.vol`); else THIN when volume is live and `this_vol < thin_ratio × B.vol`; else RECYCLE.

**Volume NA.** A bar is NA when its session is not the front month (`front_month == 0` in the 1-minute file) or its volume is 0. A visit is NA if any of its bars is; the first visit's NA flag never changes. NA makes ACCEPTED time-only, THIN unavailable, the HUNT burst skipped and R4 skipped. Because `fm_na` folds the front-month flag in, two visits with live volume are always in the same volume regime, so a cross-regime ratio cannot be computed by construction.

`leave_vol_ok` (the R4 of a LEAVE read): per-bar mean volume of the far-side closes since R1 ≥ the sit's per-bar mean; `null` when either side is NA; re-evaluated on every far-side bar.

---

## 8. The gate at a Foundation SETUP

Evaluated on the SETUP bar k with direction S, after the watch step of that bar. The ledger row is created first with the card's columns; on a LEAVE read it also records the entered band (`entered_zone_id`, `entered_visit_n`, `entered_read` = that band's read as if it were the ref band).

1. **A REENTER already decided on this bar** by the watch step (R5 satisfied on the SETUP bar itself) makes the row `REENTER` with branch `watch`.
2. **Hard BLOCK**, in this order, no watch opened and any existing watch untouched: `in_position` (an FZ position is open on this bar), `clock` (bar open time ≥ `no_entry_from`), `open_pierce` (within the session's first `open_bars` bars and before `open_window_until`, the bar's range crosses an edge of a band whose last visit ended in an earlier session and that has fewer than `open_sit_closes` closes inside today), `hunt_fade` (the latest HUNT of the ref band or of the band just left, or of any band under `fade_scope = any_band`, is in S's direction, completed within `fade_block_bars`, same session), `new` (the read is NEW).
3. **TAKE branches**, the first that holds:
   - **leave**: read LEAVE, S equals the leave side, `leave_vol_ok` is not False, not a gap LEAVE inside the first `open_quiet_bars` bars, and `leave_far_side`: `any` accepts; `block_list` refuses when the entered band reads RECYCLE, THIN, HUNT or REJECT (`block_reason = leave_into_recycle`); `no_band` refuses whenever a band contains the close (`leave_into_band`). A refusal records `take_why` and falls through to WATCH.
   - **first_print**: read FIRST_PRINT, the visit is at least `first_print_min_bars` old, S equals the visit's `entry_dir`.
   - **defend**: read ACCEPTED and the ref band's latest HUNT or latest REJECT (one slot each, §6) fell in this visit, within `defend_window_bars`, at the edge S points away from.
   - A **leave** TAKE of the band a watch waits on, in the watch's direction, is that watch's REENTER instead (branch `leave`, `reenter_reason = take_on_watch:leave`); a first_print or defend TAKE stays Foundation's own position and leaves the watch as it is.
   - A TAKE calls `open_position('TAKE')`; the engine may have skipped the SETUP for a wrong-side stop, in which case the row records `refused` and no position opens. An opposite-direction TAKE ends an open watch (`opposite_take`). A converted (branch-1) REENTER that the callback refuses keeps `gate = REENTER` with `refused` set and no position, and its `outcome_gate` is then REENTER too; this has not occurred on the tape (0 rows in all four strategies), and what it should become is open (S44 b).
4. **WATCH_EDGE**: `edge_watch = ref_band`, the read is PENDING, the previous close was inside the ref band and S is the side the close is on: a watch on the ref band that is already armed (this bar is R1).
5. **WATCH**: a band contains the close: a watch on that band with `dir = S`, not armed.
6. **BLOCK `new`** otherwise.

One watch at a time: a later SETUP that opens a watch replaces the current one (`outcome = replaced`); a BLOCKed SETUP leaves it untouched. `gate` on the row is the decision as of the SETUP bar (what the truncation test compares); `outcome_gate` is how the SETUP ended (REENTER when a later REENTER used this SETUP as its R5), and the tables and headline counts use `outcome_gate`.

---

## 9. The watch machine

A watch pins a snapshot of its band (edges, mid, the sit's per-bar mean volume) and runs once per bar before the gate, from the bar after it opened.

- **Cancels**, checked first: the first bar of a new session (`session_end`); `leave_closes` consecutive closes beyond the band on the side opposite to the watch direction (`opposite_leave`); from ARMED, `cancel_inside_bars` consecutive closes back inside (`back_inside`). An opposite TAKE cancels from the gate (`opposite_take`).
- **R1**: a close beyond the band on the watch's side arms the watch (`armed_at`; `first_armed_at` on the first arming). A close back inside breaks the far-side run; the next far-side close arms again (R1 again), so R3 (no close inside or across the mid since R1) holds by construction on the unbroken run. The ledger reports both `armed_bars` (from the first arming) and `rearmed_bars` (from the latest).
- **R2**: `leave_closes` consecutive far-side closes. **R4**: per-bar mean volume of the far-side run ≥ the pinned sit mean, skipped (None) when the run or the sit is volume-NA. `r4_bars_evaluated / fail / na` are counted per window.
- **R5**: a Foundation SETUP in the watch direction on this bar or on the previous bar of the same session.
- **REENTER** on the first bar j where R1–R5 hold, unless the bar's open time is at or past `no_entry_from` (`clock_1520` counted, watch stays armed) or a position is open (`reenter_in_position`). The callback prices nothing back; it may refuse (`wrong_side_stop`, `sl_dead_at_fill`), counted as `reenter_refused`, the watch continues. On success the row of the R5 SETUP gets `fill_bar`, `fill_used` (`setup_close` when j is the SETUP bar, else `reenter_close`), `fill_delay_bars`, `edge_dist_pts`, `armed_bars`, `rearmed_bars`, `reenter_reason` and `outcome_gate = REENTER`.
- **Outcomes** in the watch log: `reenter`, `replaced`, `cancelled:<reason>` (never armed) or `armed_expired:<reason>` (armed), `active` at the data end. `no_same_dir_setup` counts armed watches that expired with R1–R4 satisfied on their last bar.

Position lifetime is entry bar ≤ k < exit bar, so a SETUP on a position's exit bar may open a new one at that bar's close; `build_trades` asserts that no two FZ positions overlap under that convention.

---
